results.quote: like counting objects, tracking arrows, or spotting a false premise
results.source_quote: Humanity's First Exam (HFE) evaluates whether frontier language and multimodal models can consistently solve elementary tasks that humans complete without specialized training: visual object counting, color and symbol identification, spatial tracking, basic arithmetic, strict formatting constraints, and false-premise verification. … Raising effort from low to high in the paper's ablations lifts Family pass⁴ by 17 to 32 percentage points on several reasoning models (and disabling thinking on Flash models drops Family pass⁴ below 10%), concentrated in symbolic text subcategories (+26.2 to +29.7 percentage points mean lift on Logical Deduction, Algorithmic and Symbolic Execution, and Constraint Satisfaction) vs. small gains on core Vision (+2.0 percentage points on Arrows/Pointers and +1.9 percentage points on Object Counting).
results.artifact_sentence: Instead of PhD-level questions, it tests simple, ninety-second tasks humans breeze through, like counting objects, tracking arrows, or spotting a false premise.

    return ctx.require('deepmind', r'visual object counting.*false-premise verification', r'Arrows/Pointers')

results.quote: it measures floor reliability, asking whether a model solves four slightly varied versions of a task consistently across repeated tries

results.artifact_sentence: And it measures floor reliability, asking whether a model solves four slightly varied versions of a task consistently across repeated tries.
